d.subject: CONFIRMED dual WakeInner race: transition generation is not a valid async effect lifetime
d.head: 98a7c1cde9fd36d47562b40fa25ed0b094038e70
d.finding: WakeInner is emitted on NATIVE_COVER->OPENING_FROM_CLOSED with controller generation G and launched asynchronously. Normal OPENING_FROM_CLOSED->INNER_HANDOFF progression increments generation before the IO worker necessarily starts, so a valid wake can be suppressed. Conversely, if the worker starts before a genuine reversal advances generation, the physical wake can reach setDisplayPowerMode while final semantics return to native cover. Same semantic input therefore depends on thread schedule.
d.physicalMutation: DuoShellService.wakeInnerPhysicalDisplay resolves 1968x2184 physical inner and invokes hidden SurfaceControl.setDisplayPowerMode(token,2); current shell source has one setDisplayPowerMode call and no explicit inner OFF counterpart.
d.recommendedInvariant: Use semantic openingAttemptId/wakeIntent lifetime spanning normal handoff; revoke on reversal/reset/privilege loss/destroy/new attempt/inner-active; atomic one-shot commit immediately before shell wake. When a reversal is already in the same drained batch, consume the batch before queueing the worker.
d.next: Production-level controlled wake executor/facade integration test at current main; no production change authorized here.
d.en: Confirmed at Alpha3 HEAD: the asynchronous physical inner wake is keyed to controller transition generation, but normal opening handoff increments that generation. This can drop a valid wake if IO starts late, while an early IO start can leak a wake across a reversal. The shell wake is a real physical-panel power-mode mutation. Use a semantic opening-attempt token plus batch-final commit gating; no physical Fold7 occurrence is claimed.
